outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms a CUA is required, file the CUA application after the pre-application meeting. What to say: Frame it as a bar use in the Castro NCD. Emphasize standard hours (6 a.m.–2 a.m.), food with limited cooking, recorded music only (no live entertainment or dancing), and no outdoor seating. Commit to soundproofing so noise and bass are inaudible beyond premises, posted patron notices at entrances, daily sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, garbage kept inside, appointing a community liaison, and transparency for law enforcement. If merging storefronts, explain how it serves the neighborhood mix. Include letters from the Castro Merchants Association, Castro LGBTQ Cultural District, and nearby businesses. Attach acoustical plans or commit to an acoustic study.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Attend the mandatory community meeting and Planning Commission hearing; respond to requests for additional information. What to say: At the community meeting, explain the operating plan, hours, noise mitigation, and patron management. Listen to neighbor concerns and incorporate feedback where feasible (earlier weeknight closing, extra soundproofing, shared sidewalk cleaning). At the hearing, testify the concept contributes to the Castro's mix, will not expand into outdoor areas or late-night hours, and will comply with standard bar conditions in the NCD. Bring the community liaison and support letters. If the Commission requests conditions (noise monitoring, annual reporting, occupancy cap), agree on the record.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the CUA is approved, obtain the Planning Commission Motion and file for the ABC license with the lease, entity formation, and seller's permit. What to say: Submit the ABC application with the approved Motion as zoning sign-off, signed lease, entity proof (Articles of Organization), seller's permit from CDTFA, and ABC forms and fees. Post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days. If the census tract shows undue concentration, prepare a Public Convenience or Necessity letter with Planning and Police explaining how the bar serves the entertainment corridor and complies with all conditions. ABC refers the application to Planning and Police; respond promptly to follow-up questions.
outcomes.note: The record shows only density statistics; it does not state the filing procedures, document requirements, or ABC referral process.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (BAN) and file a Fictitious Business Name statement if needed. What to say: Register online with the EIN, entity name, and business address to get the Business Account Number. Pay the tiered registration fee based on projected gross receipts. File the DBA statement with the County Clerk in person or by mail, publish once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper, and file proof of publication within 45 days. The filed DBA is needed for the bank account and ABC application.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application for the kitchen and bar areas with drawings, equipment layout, finishes, and menu. What to say: Submit two sets of scaled drawings showing kitchen layout, bar area, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, prep surfaces, refrigeration, hood (if any), and restrooms, plus the menu and preparation narrative. Route the plan check with the building permit so DPH is a reviewing station. Pay the plan-check fee (for a bar with limited cooking, likely $828–$1,241). Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction and a final pre-opening inspection at least two weeks before opening. Ensure a certified food safety manager is on staff before final inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements: architectural plans, mechanical plans for hood and HVAC, plumbing for sinks and grease interceptor, and electrical plans. What to say: Submit stamped architectural plans showing the bar, kitchen, restrooms, ADA upgrades, and any structural or finish work. outcomes.original: Filing step: After the building permit and ABC license are issued and the final DPH inspection passes, apply for the Health Permit to Operate and any required music licenses (ASCAP, BMI). What to say: Submit the Health Permit application online with the BAN, Location ID, and federal tax ID, attaching proof of the certified food safety manager and approved DPH plan check. Schedule the final pre-opening inspection; the inspector confirms the facility matches plans, all equipment is installed, hand sinks have soap and towels, and hot water is available. Pay the $470 permit fee. Once issued, the business may serve food and drinks to the public. Sign up for ASCAP and BMI licenses online; annual fee is formula-based on occupancy and music use (typically $300–$2,500 each).

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: These ranges are for the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost and fee waivers) and the Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000), the approvals in the entitlement path given by the rules. The ranges are times to approval when those approvals are granted, not times to denial or withdrawal. The CUA timeline includes pre-application meeting, community meeting, environmental review, Planning Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period; the Castro Theatre CUA filed June 2022 was approved June 2023 (353 days), but that case included Planning Code text amendments and Article 10 review. A bar CUA without legislation or historic review typically takes 6–10 months. The ABC license is not in the entitlement path (insufficient-information status), but when alcohol type and transaction are known, budget 60–240 days and $1,000–$450,000 depending on license type. The building permit (14–120 days, $800–$15,000) runs in parallel or after the CUA; DBI cannot issue it until Planning signs off on the approved CUA. DPH plan check (21–60 days, $828–$2,500) is a prerequisite for the health permit and routes with the building permit. Total calendar time from filing the CUA to opening is typically 8–14 months when a CUA is granted and construction is straightforward, but confirming the zoning determination in writing before filing is critical because no time or cost should be incurred if Planning determines the concept is not permitted as described.
